subject: Data incident cap / security exhibit — proposal for Acme counter
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Chen <mchen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redline — data incident cap

Michael — quick update from Acme legal: they have redlined our standard MSA/Order Form to remove the limitation of liability for data incidents entirely and want an explicit carve-out that makes breach-related damages uncapped for "compromise of Acme customer data." Sales pushed back but Customer insists this is non-negotiable for their board.

I need legal's recommendation on an acceptable commercial compromise to keep this deal moving. Options I see:
- Propose a breach-specific sublimit (e.g., fixed dollar cap) tied to the security addendum;
- Offer a waterfall: remediation costs (unlimited), statutory fines/taxes limited to X, other damages capped at Y;
- Keep liability cap but add negligence/intent carveout language limited to proven willful misconduct.

Attached: my redline of the Order Form with Acme's comments (OrderForm_REDLINE.docx). Can legal draft 1–2 alternate redline options we can price to the customer? Need this before EOD Monday so sales can present at Tuesday exec review.

Thanks,
Mina
Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_REDLINE.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 06 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redline — data incident cap

Thanks Mina — read Acme's counter. High level thoughts: we should avoid an uncapped exposure for security incidents. Typical commercial compromises that balance customer comfort and our risk appetite:

1) Security exhibit + defined breach sublimit: set a separate sublimit for security incidents tied to the security addendum (e.g., $3M or a multiple of monthly fees). This preserves a cap while acknowledging the increased sensitivity of data incidents.

2) Waterfall allocation language: pay remediation costs (reasonable and documented) first (not subject to cap), with other consequential or punitive damages limited to the sublimit. This keeps remediation (forensics/notification) out of the cap, but caps other categories.

3) Statutory fines / regulatory penalties: we should resist uncapped indemnity for fines unless customer agrees to include indemnity for third-party claims only where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct is proven.

Draft suggestion: add a Security Exhibit that defines "Security Incident" and an Order Form clause that sets a Security Event Sublimit equal to the lesser of (a) $3,000,000 and (b) 12 months of committed Fees; remediation and notification costs are reimbursed outside the Sublimit. Also include a clause requiring customer to mitigate and cooperate.

I'm attaching a working draft of the Security Addendum and a redline snippet for the Order Form. If legal + commercial are aligned I can send to Acme with a clear commercial fallback (e.g., $1.5M / 6 months fees).

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Security_Addendum_v2.docx (docx, 52KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redline — data incident cap

Appreciate the options — banding a sublimit to months-of-fees is something Acme might accept if we can show it's predictable and ties to their scale. Two quick asks:
- Can you convert the proposal into two concrete redline alternatives we can price: (A) $3M / 12 mo fallback, (B) $1.5M / 6 mo fallback?
- Can you add an explicit sentence that remediation (forensics, reasonable notification costs, credit monitoring) is outside the Sublimit? Acme is sensitive to customer remediation costs and needs to see those are covered.

I'll prep commercial impact numbers for Lauren to review and will loop in finance if we land on the $3M path. Goal: present both options to Acme legal on Wednesday.

Thanks — Mina

From: Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redline — data incident cap

Quick commercial note from my side: any proposal that meaningfully increases expected loss for the account will need an offset (discount reduction or term shortening). $3M sits well for larger enterprise deals but will materially change margin on this one unless we tie it to committed ARR or a higher fee.

Suggested commercial structure to present to Acme:
- Option A (standard risk): security sublimit = lesser of $1.5M or 6 months' fees (no change to price).
- Option B (premium protection): security sublimit = lesser of $3M or 12 months' fees, with 12% uplift on list pricing OR a 24-month firm term commitment.

If legal can draft the two redlines Karthik suggested, we'll price both and present them as tradeoffs. I want the security addendum to be explicit that remediation costs are outside the cap and that the sublimit only covers direct damages arising from the incident (not consequential/punitive).

-Lauren
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Chen <mchen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form redline — data incident cap

Michael — per our internal alignment, attached are two formal redline options for the Order Form and a clean Security Addendum for your review:

Option 1 (conservative): Security Event Sublimit = the lesser of $1,500,000 and six (6) months of Committed Fees; remediation costs (forensics, notification, credit monitoring) are excluded from the Sublimit and reimbursed on a documented basis. Redwood's liability for statutory/regulatory fines remains subject to proof of Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Option 2 (sponsor): Security Event Sublimit = the lesser of $3,000,000 and twelve (12) months of Committed Fees; requires either a 12% list price uplift while retaining a 12-month term or a 24-month committed term at current pricing. Same remediation-cost carve-out and cooperation requirements apply.

Attached: OrderForm_REDLINE.docx, Security_Addendum_v2.docx. If Acme is comfortable with Option 1 we can proceed quickly; if you prefer Option 2 please confirm commercial uplift or term length and we'll update the Order Form.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_REDLINE.docx (docx, 75KB); Security_Addendum_v2.docx (docx, 60KB)
